plans.note: Section 7 is captioned 'Limitations of Liability' — check cap amount, mutuality (likely one-sided in Contractor's favour) and carve-outs for IP infringement, confidentiality breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct and indemnity obligations.

Section 7 heading refers only to 'Indemnification of Contractor', i.e. an indemnity running from us to RadialSpark. A Vendor-side indemnity for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct appears absent; also confirm nothing in sec-5 warranties supplies one, and test the breadth of the customer indemnity.

No covenant-style section in the outline; scan the purpose/engagement scope (sec-1) and any surviving covenants in sec-6 for restrictions on our business or competing products before concluding it is absent.
Check sec-1 (purpose/engagement) for any 'sole provider' or exclusive engagement language and sec-3 for compensation tied to exclusivity; otherwise absent, which favours us and needs no comment.
Pricing sits in sec-3; look for any most-favoured-customer/best-terms wording running against us. MFN in our favour would be acceptable and should not be flagged.

Consulting agreements often bury a no-hire in the termination or general covenants; check sec-6 survival language. If present, confirm duration, scope limited to individuals involved in the Services, and a general-advertising carve-out.

Section 6 governs termination — verify we have convenience termination on reasonable notice with no early-termination fee, and that Contractor cannot terminate at will mid-engagement; note any wind-down payment obligations in sec-3.

Term/renewal mechanics would appear in sec-1 or sec-6 (or an unnumbered term section between sec-1 and sec-3). If the engagement is a fixed-scope consultancy with no auto-renewal, record as not applicable rather than a deviation.

No general/miscellaneous section appears in the outline; governing law and venue may sit in an unextracted tail section. Confirm the full document before marking missing — accepted fora are NY, DE, CA or England and Wales, with courts rather than offshore arbitration.

Assignment/change-of-control language is not visible in the outline; check the end of sec-6 and any miscellaneous provisions. We need affiliate and successor assignment rights and no Vendor termination on our change of control.

Section 4 ('Ownership of Materials Related to Services; Acceptance') is the primary location — confirm work product and deliverables vest in Clear Capital, that our pre-existing IP and data are not assigned or licensed to Contractor, and check any Contractor background-IP retention.

Any licence-back or licence of Contractor background/tooling will sit in sec-4; test that it extends to our affiliates and contractors, is perpetual/irrevocable for delivered materials, and is not revocable at will.

Look for records-inspection language in sec-3 (compensation/invoicing). If an audit right against us exists, check frequency, notice, off-site review and Vendor-borne cost; audit rights in our favour are not flagged.
Check sec-3 for late-payment penalties or kill fees and sec-7 for stipulated damages payable by us. Service credits or remedies running to us are welcome and should not be flagged.

Section 5 contains the Contractor warranties plus a disclaimer — assess warranty duration, conformity to Specifications, and whether the remedy is real (re-performance or refund); read together with the acceptance mechanics in sec-4 and confirm the disclaimer does not swallow the warranty.

No insurance section in the outline; check sec-5 reps and sec-7 for any coverage undertaking. If Contractor personnel touch our data or premises, propose standard commercial, professional liability and cyber coverage.

Review sec-3 for minimum hours, retainer or take-or-pay style commitments and sec-1 for guaranteed volume of Services; if a minimum exists, confirm it terminates on our exercise of termination rights in sec-6.

Section 6 should carry post-termination effects and sec-4 the return/delivery of materials; confirm whether return of Clear Capital data and materials plus reasonable transition assistance is covered, and treat as missing only if neither section addresses it.
